messages = []

import sys

lines = sys.stdin.read().splitlines()

def compile_pattern(pattern, ignore_case):
    parts = []
    for ch in pattern:

        elif ch == '?':

        else:

    statements.append((compile_pattern(action, True), compile_pattern(resource, False)))

title: Types of Analytics: Descriptive, Diagnostic, Predictive and Prescriptive
summary: Analytics is commonly grouped into four types by the question it answers. Descriptive analytics tells you what happened, diagnostic analytics explains why it happened, predictive analytics estimates what is likely to happen, and prescriptive analytics recommends what to do about it. Most data-analyst work is descriptiv

title: Data splits and leakage
summary: Leakage lets information unavailable at prediction time influence training or evaluation. The evaluation partition must represent the deployment boundary rather than an arbitrary set of rows.

title: Attention heads, causal masks and KV sharing
summary: Multi-head attention uses several learned projections to represent different interaction patterns. Causal masks prevent a decoder position from reading future positions. Multi-query and grouped-query variants share key/value representations across query heads in different ways to reduce cache and bandwidth requirements

title: Position information and RoPE
summary: Attention without position information does not inherently encode the order of input tokens. Transformers add or otherwise incorporate position signals. Rotary position embeddings apply position-dependent rotations to query/key components, making relative position differences influence their dot products.

title: Query, key, value and scaled attention
summary: Queries represent what a position seeks; keys support matching; values provide content to combine. Scaled dot-product attention turns query-key compatibility into normalized weights and uses them to aggregate values. Attention weights are contextual computation, not a universal explanation of model decisions.

        best = max(best, right - left + 1)

title: Variables, Dynamic Typing and Object References
summary: In Python a variable is a name that refers to an object stored in memory. Assignment binds a name to an object; it never copies the object. Python is dynamically typed, meaning the type belongs to the object and is checked at run time, so the same name can refer to an int now and a string later.
